question: What is the primary anatomical destination for formulas delivered via a gastrostomy tube?
explanation: A gastrostomy tube is surgically placed directly through the abdominal wall into the stomach chamber. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is enteral nutrition via gastrostomy generally preferred over parenteral nutrition when the digestive tract works?

options.A: It preserves gut mucosal integrity and barrier function
options.B: It digests foods much faster than normal chewing
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of aspiration pneumonia
options.D: It requires sterile central venous line insertion daily

explanation: Using the natural digestive tract maintains mucosal immunity and prevents bacterial translocation from the gut. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which gastrostomy device lies flat against the abdominal wall and is often chosen for active patients?

options.B: Standard PEG tube with rigid bolster

explanation: Low-profile button devices minimize snagging on clothing and offer increased mobility for active individuals. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: What holds a standard percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy tube securely inside the gastric lumen?

options.A: Adhesive tape wrapped tightly on the abdomen
options.B: Sutures tied tightly around the outer skin
options.C: An internal retention bolster or balloon
options.D: Gravity pulling down against the stomach wall

explanation: An internal bumper or water-filled balloon prevents the tube from accidentally pulling out of the stomach. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: At what angle should the head of the bed be maintained during and after a gastrostomy feeding?
explanation: Elevating the head of the bed uses gravity to prevent regurgitation and aspiration of stomach contents into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h3)

question: A nurse auscultates the abdomen of a patient with a gastrostomy tube before feeding. What is the main purpose of this action?

options.A: To confirm the presence of bowel sounds and motility
options.B: To test for upper airway respiratory congestion
options.C: To measure the exact pH of the gastric contents
options.D: To check if the internal balloon is fully inflated

explanation: Bowel sounds indicate that the gastrointestinal tract is active and capable of processing the administered formula. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is a key characteristic of a bolus gastrostomy feeding method?

options.A: Administration limited strictly to sterile water flushes
options.B: Slow continuous infusion running over twenty-four hours
options.C: Large volumes delivered quickly over a short duration
options.D: Continuous automated delivery using an electronic pump

explanation: Bolus feeds mimic normal meals by giving larger amounts of formula over a brief period, usually 15 to 20 minutes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: When is an electric infusion pump typically selected for delivering gastrostomy nutrition?

options.A: When the nurse needs to finish all medications in under two minutes
options.B: When bolus feedings are too cheap for the hospital pharmacy budget
options.C: When the patient requires slow, continuous delivery to improve tolerance
options.D: When the patient wants to ambulate freely without any equipment

explanation: Continuous pumps are used when patients struggle to tolerate rapid volume loads in their stomach. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of flushing a gastrostomy tube with water after administering a feed?

options.A: To cool down warm formula before it enters the gastric lumen
options.B: To test if the internal retention balloon has ruptured
options.C: To rapidly rehydrate the patient through the stomach lining
options.D: To prevent formula buildup and subsequent tube clogging

explanation: Water flushes clear residual thick formula from the inner walls of the tube, keeping the lumen patent. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which cleansing agent should nurses generally avoid when performing routine care on a healed gastrostomy stoma site?

options.B: Warm tap water and mild soap
options.C: Clean soft washcloths and air drying

explanation: Harsh chemicals like hydrogen peroxide can destroy healthy granulation tissue and impede the healing process. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why should sustained-release or enteric-coated tablets never be crushed for gastrostomy administration?

options.A: Altering their form destroys their specialized release mechanism
options.B: The nursing pharmacist charges extra fees for crushed pills
options.C: Crushed pills taste extremely bitter if they touch the tongue
options.D: They will instantly dissolve into clear liquid without water

explanation: Crushing enteric-coated or sustained-release drugs causes a dangerous rapid surge of medication absorption into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h6)

question: A nurse prepares to give three different liquid medications through a gastrostomy tube. What is the correct technique?

options.A: Crush all three tablets together and stir them into cold fruit juice
options.B: Administer each medication separately with water flushes between them
options.C: Infuse all medications at once without any water flushes in between
options.D: Mix all three medications together into the hanging formula bag

explanation: Giving drugs separately and flushing between them prevents adverse drug-drug interactions and avoids tube clogs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h6)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a patient develops coughing and shortness of breath during a gastrostomy feed?

options.B: Inject 50 mL of air into the tube
options.C: Increase the pump rate to finish faster
options.D: Lower the head of the bed flat

explanation: Coughing and dyspnea suggest potential pulmonary aspiration, requiring immediate cessation of the feed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary cause of a clogged gastrostomy tube?

options.A: Using warm water instead of cold water for flushes
options.B: Rotating the external retention bolster every morning
options.C: Inadequate flushing or unapproved crushed medications
options.D: Leaving the head of the bed elevated at 45 degrees

explanation: Formula residue accumulation and poorly dissolved medications are the leading causes of mechanical tube occlusion. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is accidental dislodgement of a gastrostomy tube considered an urgent clinical situation for home caregivers?

options.A: The stoma tract can begin to close rapidly within hours
options.B: The patient will immediately starve to death in ten minutes
options.C: Formula will explode across the room from gastric pressure
options.D: Insurance companies will cancel coverage for a new tube

explanation: Gastrostomy tracts heal and contract quickly, making prompt replacement essential to keep the route open. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: What method best ensures that a family caregiver has truly mastered gastrostomy tube care before discharge?

options.A: Handing them a pre-printed pamphlet on discharge day
options.B: Verbal confirmation that they watched an online video
options.C: Requiring a hands-on return-demonstration of the skills
options.D: Asking the caregiver to read a twenty-page textbook chapter

explanation: Return-demonstration allows the nurse to directly observe technique and correct any errors before home management begins. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)
